  {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"FAQPage","mainEntity":[{"@type":"Question","name":"How do I make a polaroid style photo online for free?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"I use AdBorder (adborder.top) for this -- I upload my photo, select the Polaroid preset style, adjust the border width if I want, optionally enable Drop Shadow for added realism, and download as a PNG. The entire process takes me under 10 seconds, requires no software installation, and adds no watermark to my output."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"What is the correct polaroid border ratio?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"What I love about the classic Polaroid format is the asymmetrical border: equal-width borders on the left, right, and top sides, with the bottom border approximately three times thicker. I tested about twenty different bottom-to-side ratios before settling on this 1:1:1:3 proportion, which replicates the look of original Polaroid SX-70 instant film where the thicker bottom area housed the chemical developer pod. This is the proportion that makes a Polaroid-style frame instantly recognizable."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"What types of photos look best with a polaroid effect?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"In my experience, portraits, travel shots, street photography, and candid moments look best with a Polaroid effect because the white frame and warm tones enhance the nostalgic, personal feeling of these images. The best Polaroid-style photo I ever made was a candid shot of my sister laughing in a diner booth. I have found that landscapes and architecture photos are less ideal since the thick bottom border can disrupt the visual balance of wide, horizontal compositions."}}]}
